Saw this Sunlite Sports High-Density EVA-Foam Dumbbell Set and had to grab it. We have not been back in the pool yet - while we live in a warm weather state, we are still waiting for the pool to be warm enough - but once that day comes, we are grabbing this set and using it! It comes in a nice enough box you could use it as a gift for someone with a great pool and desire to use their time for working out with low impact movements. The set is a great set up - not just one, but three ways to help the workout. The two hand "weights" allow for resistance to mimic a weightlifting experience. They feel totally light, but significant and should give excellent resistance once in the water. The waist piece is adjustable - my wife had it on, but I did not. Do check the measurements to make sure it'll fit you. She had it on and said it was easy to adjust and felt fine - comfortable even. Can't wait to see how well it supports us in the water. There are also 2 gloves for helping with swim strokes - she's been swimming laps whoever we are in the water and I think these are going to up her game. I do less laps, but I too want to give these a try for efficiency and strengthening my arms and shoulders. It includes a two-sided sheet of exercises to help you get the most of the set, and with the coded chart telling you which ways each exercise helps - weight loss, low impact, strength, etc. This is a great way to know what you are achieving with that movement and can help with your goals. TIP: I took pictures of the sides so we can carry the phone with rather than the chart - but you could bring the lightly coated chart - for us the phone is always there, but you might not want to risk it getting wet. We have not used it yet - and will try to get back to tell you how it goes when we do - but for now we are impressed enough with this Sunlite Sports High-Density EVA-Foam Dumbbell Set that we cannot wait to get back into the water and start using it! It seems like quality material with enough options to help us workout in an efficient, effective, and fin way, getting more out of our pool time.

It comes with a sturdy retractable table tennis net that expands to 6 feet, two paddles, a mesh storage bag and three ping pong balls. Everything is amazingly sturdy- wood paddles with nice rubber coverings, balls that don't dent and a well made net that expands and pulls out of 2 strong plastic cylinder posts. For easy set up, you clamp down one post on the table, pull the net across and clamp down the other end. The sturdy clamps don't move making the net completely stable.

Playing on any table makes this so much fun. We played on a low long rectangular table in front of the couch, our oval dinner table, a card table and a long folding table. The long folding table was the closest thing to a regular game of table tennis and everyone loved the exercise they got running a bit as this was played outdoors. The oval table was shorter and there was no running but laughing, as keeping it on the table took some skill. The most laughing we had, was playing table tennis on the low coffee table in front of the couch. We were on our knees and could only tap the ball lightly to keep it on the table. When we are on our knees, you can't run after a loose ball, so we sort of end up rolling around the floor to get the ball and end up looking like we are balls on the floor. We ended up laughing more than playing on this low coffee table.

This game is well made, you can set it up on any table 6 feet wide or less, you'll get some physical exercise, lots of fun and if you play it on an odd table- lots of laughs. We could never fit a table tennis table in our small house, so this is really great that we can enjoy the game without the large table. You can't beat the price for the enjoyment this set brings to family members and friends of all ages and for that it deserves 5 Stars.

WINGET 100% Carbon Fiber Cross X Country Ski Poles XC-100 I bought these intended to just use the baskets, handles and straps on another pole. I couldn't imagine the pole was very good, but I was pleasantly surprised. There are in fact 100% carbon as best I can tell. They are extremely stiff. Stiffer than my Rex R3 poles which set me back $150. They are heavier both in weight and noticeably in swing weight. I would suggest that these poles are equivalent to a $100 all carbon pole from Swix or Rex. I imagine that these were made by a manufacturer in China that produces for a name brand and then made these afterward. The only thing these poles lack is a brand. These are great workhorse poles for an experienced skier to use for rollerskiing or for sprint races (due to their stiffness). These would be a major upgrade for anyone who doesn't have 100% carbon poles. They probably aren't the best poles for marathons where an extremely light Swix pole would be better (but also cost north of $200).

GENSUNS Yoga Balance Board, Non-Slip Surface, with Hand-Grabbing Holes, Exercise Coordination and Balance Ability of The Body We have a two piece core trainer one stands on on top of a cushion - I love this, it makes my wife uncomfortable. So when I saw this yoga core balance board I decided to give it a try.

I cannot and will not recommend it.

First, it arrived undone. There are little holes around the bottom with clips that snap into place to hold the top to the bottom. One was not in at all the another was not even halfway in. We attempted to snap them in, but could not budge them. The surface was therefore off, as you see in one picture, we could pull it easily away.

Second, for something that calls itself non-slip this is completely slippery. We both stood on it with no socks, socks, and shoes and not one felt non-slippery and in fact we had to hold onto one another and a hard, sturdy surface not to fall. With or without the top secure, the actual surface of the piece is very slippery. There are ridges, but they do nothing to provide any sort of non-slippery surface. It’s very smooth and slick.

Last, the materials themselves seem okay, but by no means strong enough to last a long time. The pieces that snap in - by virtue they are already not in - seemed like they could snap if we fought to get them in. We did try - they did not snap - but there was no way to do it. They would not snap. Does that mean the material is strong? No, we don’t think so. We think it’s just how it was made - we are still not sure one of the snap pieces even exists - we can’t see it at all.

Overall this is a nice idea, but horrible execution and a bad product. I will not and cannot recommend.

text_fidelity_a:
Under Armour Dominate 24 Ounce Vacuum Insulated Stainless Steel Bottle with Flip Top Lid Original Review (5 Stars):
I bought a pair of these in Indigo and Silver for my wife and I a couple months ago. We filled them with margaritas and took them to the beach. ;-) They worked beautifully. Now, we used them as overnight water bottles. I fill them about half way with ice then top with water, and they are still icy the next morning, and sometimes even the next day after work (about 18 hours later). The flip-up lid is great for 1-handed use. The little plastic ring, while looking a little weak, has actually stood up very well. The rubber grip and otherwise textured surface makes them easy to hang onto during long walks. I've never had the slightest problem with leaking or spilling. We absolutely love these, and will continue using them daily for years to come.

Update, reduced rating to 3 Stars:
My wife and I have been using these bottles daily for about two and-a-half years. After about a year, both bottles' vacuum seals failed, so water will no longer stay cold overnight, even when filled completely with ice right before bedtime. They also sweat almost immediately after filling. For the price, I'm really not thrilled that these didn't last longer. Further, the seal between the cap and bottle has proven to be less than adequate, as it lets some moisture out into the cap's threads every day. I have an older model Thermos with a screw top which came with a much better seal, that's still good after 5+ years, plus its vacuum seal is still intact despite being dropped several times.
text_fidelity_b: Under Armour Dominate 24 Ounce Vacuum Insulated Stainless Steel Bottle with Flip Top Lid

The price was right and the quality seems good. I like the fact that it is covered with a rubbery material that keeps it from scratching my bike.

The mount for the bike is fine but its a bit of effort to get the cable secured with the lock in such a way that it does not interfere with riding. On my bike I have a basket and usually throw the lock in the basket in transit so this is not such a problem for me.

We bought two of these locks. One for me and one for my partner. He dropped the key for his in the water beside our boat at the dock which means he is down to one key.

I saw this lock on sale on Amazon the other day for about $20 but did not order another one like I should have. If it goes on sale again Ill get my partner another lock and use his old one to lock a shopping cart to the door handle of one of those people who take up two parking places to protect their beautiful cars from the unwashed masses. For this alternative application a spare key, or even one key, would not be necessary.

Update October 9: As I mentioned above my partner dropped one of the keys for his lock into the water beside our boat. When the folks at Via Velo read my review they immediately contacted me for my mailing address and the key code. They shipped spare keys, from China, for his lock. They work fine. I had the new keys in less than a week so now we don't have to worry about breaking out the hacksaw if my partner dropped his remaining key in the drink.

In the time since I wrote my original review I have used this lock dozens of times and when I lock my bike at the gym I look at the other bikes with the $100 locks on them and cant see the difference between those and my Via Velo lock. When you add to the quality of the product the obvious commitment to customer service this company has, I am enthusiastic about what other products these folks might offer.
text_fidelity_b: Bike U Lock with Cable - Via Velo Bike Lock Heavy Duty Bicycle U-Lock,14mm Shackle and 10mm x1.8m Cable with Mounting Bracket for Road Bike Mountain Bike Electric Bike Folding Bike

text_fidelity_a: Nappaglo Bike Handlebar Grips Ergonomic Desgin, with Bilaterally Locking Ring Non-Slip for Standard Bike Grip Diameter 22.2mm These grips definitely relieve pressure by giving more surface area to the palm and repositioning the wrist.  Quality of construction appears quite good, and I’m positive they’d be great on a hybrid that you’re riding on paved/smooth surfaces.  However, there is a tradeoff if you’re using them on a mountain bike and riding any kind of rugged terrain: you will feel each and every bump transmitted straight up your arms due to the fact that your palm is now the primary point of contact.  Whether it’s something tolerable long-term, I can’t say; it’s my initial reaction after a fair ride on rocky trail.  The gain of comfort on relatively smooth stretches of trail may be worth suffering the bone-rattling over more unforgiving terrain.  It may be that I end up putting these on my hybrid for long-distance comfort and going back to round grips on my 29er.  Also, I suspect that if your hands are wide, you’ll eventually take issue with the grip ends.

Load 300lbs, Zero Stretch Jump Mat) (Green) For many people this will be the perfect mini trampoline and I have to say that I am very impressed with the quality so far. For me personally the only thing I would like is if the handle bar or stability bar was a little more...well, stable.  It fastens into two brackets (the brackets are fastened to two of the legs of the trampoline) with those little pop out pins... you know the kind you squeeze to push them down and then the bar can be pushed into the bracket and then the pins pop out through little holes to hold the handle bar on. Yes it holds the handle bar on but it is a little wobbly and if you have any type of stability issues already it could take a little while to build up trust.  I cannot use the trampoline without holding onto the bar and I haven’t had any problems yet but it’s just taking some time for me to trust it LOL  For the average person I doubt that this would be even a thought but like I said for me personally I would prefer the handlebar to be a little more solid feeling. Do I use it yes! Am I enjoying it yes! Will it be up for sale in six months no!  I chose this particular one because I wanted springs rather than the bungee type cords that could wear out faster  It does make a little spring noise but if you have music going you’re not going to notice it at all. The jump area was larger than expected and very nice. I am getting serious workouts on this thing with very limited movements on my part.  Putting it together was super simple it came in a taco shape and you just opened it up and then lifted the legs up and they went into place. The instructions did note to be careful when I unfolding which I did not read and I did smash my finger LOL my instructions showed a different stability bar that had bolts to hold it in.  I don’t know if that was for an older model or what but it makes me kind a wish that the handle did fasten with bolts.  Don’t be scared of my negativity though as far as the handle goes I am only reviewing this on how I feel about it for my own personal use and like I said I do have very restricted mobility and balance.  I would recommend this to others. You can get a serious workout in 20 to 30 minutes. Franklin Sports Glomax Darts Light Up Soft Toss Long dark winter days. Cabin fever. Snowed in. No activity. Kids climbing the walls. What to do...

We're all heading into the basement where we have collected fun games over the years, like an air hockey table, Foosball, electronic darts, an electronic basketball hoop....and now our new addition, the light-up lawn darts game. It is a blast in the basement (although we keep a little bit of lighting on). This is so much fun, and really adds a unique game to break up our wintertime boredom.

Here are a few tips that may help you.

1) We put a few streaks of glow-in-the-dark paint on the rings, to brighten them up a bit, and it worked wonderfully. We got this super bright green glow in the dark paint for about $10 here on Amazon and it worked great: [[ASIN:B00BD63C8W Ultra Green V10 Glow in the Dark Paint 1/2Oz]]

In fact, these lawn darts take the LR41 batteries, which you can get 10 of them from Amazon for about $6: [[ASIN:B000AQ7ME6 Maxell Watch Battery Button Cell LR41 AG3 192 Pack of 10 Batteries]]. Or if you want more, you can get 50 of them for about $13-14: [[ASIN:B0057ON2JA 50 Pack Maxell LR41 AG3 192 button cell battery "NEW HOLOGRAM PACKAGE "]] .

3) If you need replacement parts, which is honestly unlikely, as these things are sturdy as heck. And if you need information on replacement parts, you can email: replacementparts@franklinsports.com or you can call 1-781-341-5178.

Thanks for reading my review. I sure hope it helped you.

Sportline Lightweight Walking Advantage 385 Tally Counter With Easy To Read Number Display That Counts Up To 9999 Anyone working out on an indoor track will find a counter helpful. At 12 laps a mile, counting laps is difficult. Counting is easy; remembering how many laps I've done is hard.

The Sportline counter fixes what my math teacher could not, allowing me to turn my mental energies toward my workout, or toward a conversation with my running partner.

---Necessary on a Practical Level---
I tried a system of using my fingers on my right hand to measure laps 1-5, then using my left hand to measure how many laps in groups of five. That is, two fingers on my left and three fingers on my right would equal 13 laps. It sounds easier to employ than it actually is.

The Sportline counter has five worthwhile features:
* It counts one per click, up to 9,999. I won't run more than that, so, for me, it is plenty.
* The display is legible while running. The white digits are large, on a black background.
* The size of the device is small enough to carry.
* The finger loop fits nicely in my middle finger.
* The reset dial quickly zeroes out the counter.

The only two drawbacks are

text_fidelity_a:
Pflueger Patriarch LP Baitcast Reel The specs here say this is the 7.1:1 ratio version of the Patriarch. What I actually received was the PATRIARCH64LP - the 6.4:1 ratio version of the reel. I believe this is important to some people and at minimum it is incorrectly described here. I will email Amazon directly.

Now - I have to say, 6.4/7.1 - doesn't make a difference to me. I'm not good or knowledgeable enough to let it bother me. On another site it says at 7.1 you are bringing in 28" per turn. With the 6.4 it is 26" per turn. I guess I will just have to crank a little faster if I'm in a lure race.

I wanted to deduct a star for the wrong spec but I can't. The reel is too too too nice. I decided to upgrade both my ultralight spinner (old Browning) and baitcaster (Abu 5500C) and settled on the Patriarch spinner and baitcaster. New rods too. I've been an on/off angler for about 20 years mostly from the shore in rivers and lakes. Now I live on the river.

This is an early review - one day (few hours) of use. I spooled up some 15 lb fluorocarbon line, put on a heavy Poe's diver and headed out to the dock. To start I had the dial up to 10 and the brake so I had to jiggle the rod to make the lure drop. Eventually as I got a little more confident with it I backed both down. One mild rats nest during the adjustment.

The feel on the rod is very nice. Compared with the 5500C this is a light and very small reel that fits beautifully in the palm of my hand. I've got it on a 7' MH rod and threw out a couple of sidearm casts. Distance wasn't great but the casts were smooth and backlash free. After each cast I dropped the brakes down a little. Eventually I went to some two-handed casts - one of which I got the mild backlash but was real happy with the distance at this point. I tried a few overhands but I need more practice as the distance was very short - like I was throwing the lure into the water.

One thing I noticed - I'm not sure if this is good or bad. My old 5500C3's eye - the part where it spreads the line evenly on the reel - would move back and forth when casting too. The Patriarch does not. I'm trying to think it through and can't really tell if there's an advantage of one over the other.

Reeling in the lure was smooth. You could feel this is a precision made reel. There was no gear rumble - smooth as glass. I was able to finely control the crankbait's depth and speed of retrieve.

By the crank is the star drag. On the 5500C I would have a little bit of a hard time adjusting the drag. The star was smaller and my fingers couldn't get much of a grip on it. The drag control on the Patriarch is big - almost kung fu weapon big. Easy to adjust but not in the way.

That's all I can say for now. I need more hours with the new reel and rod and different lures to see how it will work for me. The 5500C is a tank-like reel, big, strong and powerful. The Patriarch may have these features also but in the smaller package with the aggressive low profile shape it seems built more for finesse.

More to come... ask questions.
text_fidelity_b: Pflueger Patriarch LP Baitcast Reel

text_fidelity_a:
Monstrum Tactical MOLLE Utility Pouch Here I am again, this time I'm looking for the best pouch possible for a very specific carry option. I've wanted something to carry one of my home made mini EDC kits, plus a few other items. I've found some really nice models, but they were usually too big or too small. Some were a great size for my needs, but were cost prohibitive.

Alas, I found a Monstrum Tactical MOLLE Utility Pouch on Amazon for about $14. I had narrowed it down to this item over a Condor Gadget MOLLE Pouch. The prices were nearly identical, so I went over both items with a discerning eye. The Monstrum was about a half-inch smaller, so it was a close call.

I believe some Monstrum products mimic their higher priced competition, yet still make a great value. There may be subtle differences here and there, but there were no major must-haves. I rarely go for the high end products when I find one that is similar for a lower price and good reviews. A quick note on reviews? Take them ALL with a grain of salt.

The Monstrum pouch appears to be very well made. The stitching appears sturdy and I only found one loose thread, which I burned down in about 3 seconds. It was a small detail, but it lent itself to the overall quality. The zippers, zipper pulls, and Velcro patches are also solid.

Features on the pouch were way more than I expected and what I saw online. As I looked it over, right after opening the Amazon box, I knew I had hit a homerun. From the front, there is a hard pouch cover with a zippered pocket. On the underside of that cover is a heavy duty patch of Velcro that connects to the front, expandable, pocket. On either side of that pocket are elastic loops that can be adjusted to hold the pocket tightly closed. In this front area, you have it subdivided into different sections. Behind this front area, you have the main pocket. It has 3 subdivisions and they held everything I wanted with a tiny bit of room left. This main pocket has two zippers w/pulls. On the back of the pouch, there are two MOLLE snap straps, which are useful to wear on a belt, if you know how to weave them correctly.

One of the main things that I liked was the expandable front pocket. It really protrudes as you add more stuff, so those adjustable elastic straps help it stay secure. It more than serves its purpose.

Pros:

Skinny people may be okay walking in that heat, but not a fat person trying to lose weight!  So, for me, I have been walking slow and in short "bursts" to get acclimated and able to move up in speed and time. This treadmill is helping, but I was afraid, when I got it, that it wouldn't work well for me because I was a bit too heavy for it.  That's why I would ask that the people who make this should look into making it sturdier for those of us who are trying to improve our heath by using a treadmill. text_fidelity_a: LEE PRECISION Lee Preciesion 90999, Single Stage Press, Classic Cast Breech Lock I studied long and hard on whether to purchase this fine heavy duty Lee Cast Iron Breech lock press. I have used many presses over the last 40 years and still own some of the finest ones made. I was introduced to the unique breech-lock system 2 years with their hand press. The additional cost of bushings is somewhat of a downside but outweighed with speed of die change over. I have replaced all of Lee's rubber "O" ring lockrings due to their instability and lack of accurate repeatable settings. Hornady's  side lock clamping and Forster rings are far better and do not mar the 7/8"X14 threads due to frequent adjustments. My use of the Breech Press was another press for more mundane belling,universal decapping,expander mandrels and case forming of pistol and 300 B.O. This usage for me reduces the number of needed breech lock adapters. The only fault that I have found is that the shell holder mounting slot is pointed to the right of the press opening sharing the same slot to allow the primer kicker arm to deflect spent primers into the scrap tube. I find that by using the shell holder opening pointed to the left during use with a right mounted handle will sometimes push the shell holder to the right thus dismounting the shell holder. I wish that Lee would modify the right sided shell holder installation slot to the middle and re-mill the area and still keep the primer deflector as is.All in all 5 stars for sure and a great product. The ram is solid with no sloppiness at the top of stroke.
text_fidelity_b: LEE PRECISION Lee Preciesion 90999, Single Stage Press, Classic Cast Breech Lock

text_fidelity_a:
Nike Golf Xtreme Sport IV Golf Bag First, to establish my street cred, I'm retired and play lots of golf. Last year I played 118 rounds. I play year around and walk/carry, walk with push cart, and ride in a cart, mostly depending on weather. I need a bag that is easy to carry but also also works on carts. I like to have all my stuff with me in my bag. Rain gear, extra gloves, rangefinder, umbrella, sunscreen, water bottle, Advil, windbreaker, cigars, towels, balls, tees, etc. you get the picture.

This bag is nice looking, but after playing a few rounds with it, it seems it was designed by a designer, not a golfer. It's attractive and generally speaking, it's functional. But there are a few things I can mention that are why I'm deducting a couple stars. Golfers like me will know what I'm talking about.

The good things: I like the dividers. There are several and they keep the clubs well-separated so you can easily see each iron and don't have to shuffle the heads around to find your 9-iron. The legs pop out solidly and pop back in crisply when you pick it up. It is very, very light....so all the weight you will feel is from the stuff you load into it. The carrying straps are wide and comfortable and there is some nice padding on the side that hits your back. The insulated cooler pocket is nice, but I haven't had a chance yet to see how it does in 100 degree Texas heat. Gotta be better than nothing though right?

The issues: While not necessarily show-stoppers, these things could be better. When you load this bag onto an electric golf cart, the golf cart strap you pull around your bag to hold it on comes right across the top of two zippered pockets. In other words, if you want to get into those two pockets on your bag, you have to either a) unhook the strap holding your bag on, or b) keep those zippers halfway down to be able to get into them.

The next thing is also somewhat minor, but worth mentioning. I have a Sun Mountain Speed Cart, which is a 3-wheeled push cart you set your carry bag on when you don't to carry it. This bag is a little bigger than my old Titleist carry bag, and it doesn't "nest" into the arms of the push cart perfectly. It works, but this bag kind of sits a little awkwardly in the Speed Cart.

The zippers. The reason I needed a new bag was that the nylon zippers on my old bag finally failed. You know how nylon zippers will ultimately just not zip? The zipper thing goes up and down, but the two sides stay apart. Well anyway, this bag has nylon zippers too of course, and these seem to be of lighter duty than my old bag. They may end up working fine for years....but they are definitely of a smaller and more dainty construction.

Finally...the thing I am most disappointed in is the zippered pockets themselves. Remember I said this was created by a designer rather than a golfer? Well, when you unzip the pockets, you can slide your open hand in and feel both sides of the pocket pressing on your hand! It's like they are designed for small flat stuff! The big front pocket for golf balls is the only one with ample room. The others are very tight and I'm worried cramming all my stuff in there is going to put too much pressure on those dainty zippers!

The price is attractive, and hopefully it will hold up to the beating I am about to give it. If somebody reminds me in a few months, I'll update my review after putting it through the paces of several dozen rounds. Fore!
text_fidelity_b: Nike Golf Xtreme Sport IV Golf Bag

text_fidelity_a:
Stack-On PS-1520 Gun Safe I've had my safe for a couple weeks now and I am pretty happy with it. I was looking for an inexpensive safe to keep valuables away from the casual thief. This safe is not going to stop a professional thief. For that type of safe you need to pay upwards of $500. This safe is also not fire or waterproof so if you need those types of features look elsewhere.

The safe weighs about 40 pounds so it is critical to bolt it down, otherwise a thief can just walk off with it. There are 4 holes in the back of the safe and 4 holes in the bottom. There were 4 pretty hefty screws provided, I mounted my safe inside a large cabinet and it seems pretty secure. The safe and door are made of pretty heavy gauge steel so it is not going to be easy to just pry it open.

Inside the safe there are two metal shelves held in place by cheap plastic fasteners. But I will get into that later. Programming the security code was very easy and I had no problem opening and closing the safe. The safe also comes with two keys in case you forget your code or if the batteries die. There is a pretty loud beep when the buttons are pressed but that can be turned off.

I just have two minor issues with the safe. First, the cheap plastic fasteners used to hold the shelves in place are useless. When I opened the safe they were laying in the bottom of the safe with the shelves and half of them were broken. Easily resolved though, I just used metal bolts and screws I had to hold the shelves in place. I think manufacturer should provide these. The second issue I had was with the cheap shelf liners provided. They are very thin foam material and don't stay in place when sliding things in and out. Again though easily resolved by replacing with more substantial liner.

Overall I am pretty happy with this safe. I looked at others in the price range and many seemed to have significant quality issues. The issues I have with this safe are very minor and to be expected for a safe at this price point. This safe is a good value for your money as long as you are just looking to protect valuables from a casual thief
text_fidelity_b: Stack-On PS-1520 Gun Safe

Reliance Products Aqua-Tainer 7 Gallon Rigid Water Container (Pack of 2) I've owned this brand and style of water container for almost 17 years, it's my go-to for camping and day trips where there might not be any water. I have almost always had at least 2 of them, one for drinking water, the other for potable water (cleaning dishes, cooking, dog water). Recently having to purchase two more, I guess the one that's put on the age and seen places finally developed a crack on the bottom. Not bad after 7-8 years being lugged around.

Pros: Lots of water on hand - Easy to use - Stack able - Durable - Trusted brand -

Cons: Heavy once full (7gallons x 7lbs per gallon of water + container = 50lbs) - spigot almost never lines up pointing down no matter how many ways you screw on the cap - price raised by $10 in past year

Points to look at when choosing: If you can't lift 7 gallons, get the 2.5 or 5 gallon model

text_fidelity_a:
Mongoose Expo Youth Kick Scooter, Suggested for Riders with Ages 6 to 9 Years Old, Max. Weight of 175 lbs., Front and Rear Caliper Brakes, Rear Axle Pegs, 12-Inch Inflatable Wheels Definitely for a 7-11 year old. NOT big enough for an adult rider despite other reviews and weight limit..it is simply made for short kids. Assembly: Took 2 of us about an hour because of the terrible directions and lack of weird tools needed to tighten/loosen brakes. Just a PIA.

The pegs on the back wheel immediately injured my 8 year old cutting her ankle. FAIL. She is an awesome scooter connoisseur but this design just tears up your ankles. My 11 year old then tried and his sneaker got caught on the back pegs almost causing a wipeout but he ripped his sneaker free and recovered with a minor stumble. FAIL. I then removed the back pegs easily but I guess no tricks for us. My daughter then tried again and sliced up her other ankle on the exposed screw left behind from the peg attachment.

We want to like this scooter but it is made for little kids with pretty poor balance that can not use a regular scooter. We will probably keep it for now--because it is great to ride over rocks and tough terrain with the awesome bike wheel on it.

Just beware that this may not fit your needs--or may--but know what you are buying before you attempt the annoying assembly.

text_fidelity_a: Avid Elixir Caliper Service Kit I'm a diesel mechanic I work on things everyday at work. Hydraulics are something I deal with on a regular basis. I figured swapping these out would be a easy though a moderately technical adventure. So I ordered them and set them aside with my leaky brakes waited till I had a friend over whom had the same brake set. Perhaps I could teach my friend thru my rebuild in the case he needed to rebuild his in the future. So we sat down one night and went for it... I got the small air compressor from the garage and brought it into the basement shop. I figured the reviews here stated some guy mentioned the possibility of doing it  with a bike pump how bad can it be. The AVID manual makes it sound so easy. Face the caliper piston down to a rag in one hand use compressed air to unseat the piston. Well we shot 70 PSI... nope waited for it to charge some more. 90psi nope... At this point we were really struggling to hold the blow gun against the caliper and not have any leaks. So we decide the little air compressor was no longer going to pull it off. I run the air hose from my 125 psi unit in the garage. I think this time the piston will move for sure. I pin it up against the basement wall put my whole weight into the rubber tip of the blow gun. Pull the trigger, no leaks at all no movement of the piston at all. Friend decided he would try with pliers while I was off taking a leak, despite me knowing full well that it would crack with all the warnings on this site. He wound up chipping the piston. The kit looks quality as its OEM but man its really bad to install. I'm still left brainstorming ideas of how to remove the piston. I ended up getting thru the riding season this winter its going down. Almost need hydraulic pressure air compresses.
text_fidelity_b: Avid Elixir Caliper Service Kit

text_fidelity_a: Zen Posture Ume Meditation Cushion (Light Grey Side) I can't imagine that this cushion was designed by anyone who meditates for long periods.  I suppose the first clue was how the description states that with this unique design you can sit on it sideways for more lift... as if they didn't already realize that monks and meditating enthusiasts have been doing that with the traditional round cushion forever.  But I figured perhaps they meant it gave more stability than the round cushion when turning it sideways or something.  The biggest issue is the large and rough seams in the middle from where the different colored strip on top meets the sides.  Those edges might not bother anyone who does short sits, but after a long day of sitting they can take their toll on the sit bones and buns.  They put more emphasis on making this cushion look "cool" with that colored strip rather than on function.  The felt material is interesting and is probably good for making sure you don't slide off the seat like some fabrics are prone to causing.  I thought this might make a good travel cushion because it's listed as 10" x 12", but my ruler measures it as larger.  So it's going back.

text_fidelity_a:
Black Diamond Revolt Headlamp Everyone I know uses Black Diamond headlamps, but I've always owned Petzl. I've always wondered if I'd like BD better. When I had a bag stolen that had my newest Petzl headlamp in it I thought I'd try out the Black Diamond Revolt. For a headlamp that can recharge batteries with a USB cable it was a really good price, so I pulled the trigger on it. It has adequate lumens for my purposes (backpacking, evening hiking, and use around the house), although it isn't quite as bright as my similarly priced Petzl models. It has an awesome, fully adjustable dimmer setting that is the one thing that stands out as better than any other headlamp I've used. It also has a red LED setting, which is important to me - I actually find that I use the red LED way more than the white for late night use. As far as features go, I'm happy with everything you get with the Revolt.

The more I've used this headlamp though, I have a few minor complaints compared to similar offerings from Petzl. As mentioned above, I use the red LED setting often. It's great when you want to maintain night vision. I also like that if I wake up in the middle of the night and quickly use my lamp, the red LED wakes me up less than a bright white light. The problem for me is that the red setting on the Revolt is way too dim. It's hard to see anything that's more than just a few feet away. This makes it so that I can't use it in as many situations as I could with my old Petzl. I definitely wish it were brighter in the red mode.

Another feature on most headlamps is an adjustable angle setting where you can click it up and down to choose how high the lamp points. The Revolt has solid detents that seem like they will hold up well over time. This is kind of splitting hairs, but I don't like how widely spaced the detents are. It always seems to be too high or too low. YMMV, but I liked Petzl again here for the finer adjustments. I have to fiddle with the Revolt more often.

On the other hand, I'm not gentle with my headlamps. I use them constantly at home and work and any time I backpack or travel. I cram them into bags, toss them around a bit, bump them on things and occasionally drop them. It's hard to say, but friends that I work with and backpack with seem to have better luck with their Black Diamond lamps' durability. The Revolt is solidly built and seems to use batteries very efficiently. It seems like it might be a little sturdier and maybe last longer than my previous Petzl lamps, but that's purely a guess at this point. We'll see, but so far so good. I'm basing that more on friends' experiences with BD lamps. Either way, it's certainly no worse.

Overall, I think this is a pretty good headlamp. It's a solid value for the price and does everything I want it to. I'll continue to use it pretty happily, but when it comes time to replace it, I'll go back to Petzl. Even if the Revolt is a little sturdier, I like the way Petzl lamps work and feel. They're less clunky and they just seems to have their headlamps really dialed across the board. They're comfortable, intuitive and very well designed. Get a Revolt if you want a solid, functional headlamp, but get a Petzl if you really want to love it.
text_fidelity_b: Black Diamond Revolt Headlamp

Just be aware, the bathtub floor, which comes up the side, is NOT dark tech, and the rain fly is not AS dark tent as the body of the tent. Light comes through. But I can see myself laying down for an afternoon nap in it and actually not being blinded and roasted by the sun. Also I think morning wake up will be a lot gentler than morning light blasting in at dawn.

I’m pretty happy with this tent. The height on the six person is great for this older lady. It was a cinch to put up with just one person. The poles are beefier than other models and if you take care to make sure each connection is seated properly in its casing I think it will hold up. The fabric sleeves give a lot of support as you’re putting it up...not many spots where there is undo stress if you do it properly. This is a true dome tent; no “central hub”, which I can see failing almost immediately. The color is beautiful. Nice tent. Can’t wait to get out there and enjoy it.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Dark Room Sundome Camping Tent, 4/6 Person Tent Blocks 90% of Sunlight and Keeps Inside Cool, Lightweight Tent for Camping Includes Rainfly, Carry Bag, and Easy Setup

My little corner of the house where my office is can get pretty warm, but our workout bike is over here and... I turned it on and have been comfortable ever since! We'll hold onto it for just such a plan. The lit button is the on/off and works easily - click as you peddle or walk by - as I do. The clamp is wide enough to go on our handle bars, but could also mount on something like a desk or shelf, the grip strips holding it in place and enough variance of width for a few different sizes. I'd be careful not to overdo, but it should hold up to decent pressure. We have not - yet - had to charge, but it should be easy, based on what we're seeing. I'll update if anything changes in the coming months, but as of this writing, I'm comfortable, and this little DoublePlus Fan for Peloton has been a great find!

Bare Neckd Ice Cooling Towels for Athletes Sports Fitness Gym Yoga Hiking Travel Hot Flashes| Reusable Wrap Around Ice Pack Suffice to say that I have a medical condition that requires me to not get too hot. Bad things happen and they are very obvious, and not in my head. I can die if I get overheated. I just have to live with it. I also live and often work outside in one of the hottest and most humid parts of the country. Oh, and I'm not rich so I can't just hire people to do my bidding and stay inside all day. The clash of these issues has caused me to try numerous gadgets to stay cool and, honestly, this one works the best (and is one of the cheapest though it could be cheaper).

Chilling vests are ridiculously expensive and marginally effective.

"Snap towels" are a joke. Don't waste your money.

You need something with ice in it, people. And the plastic ice cubes don't work, either, and here's why: real ice melts and makes your shirt cool, too, and lasts LONGER, and is cheap.

So far this towel has worked great. I've used it a dozen times or so in very harsh conditions and bought another as a backup. You buy two dollars worth of bag ice, put it in a cooler, and you have at least two days of continuous personal cooling. The towel is long enough to fit around my big neck.

My niece tried it and told her dad she's never mowing the yard again without one. My daughter has never mowed the yard so I'm still astonished about that on two levels.

So tskile it from someone whose life and vision actually depends on staying cool (I know, sounds crazy, but it is true) : if you live in a HUMID area, this is the best balance of price and cooling you can get.

I am so serious about this product I left without it on me day and drive twenty miles back to get it, then twenty miles back to where I realized I'd forgotten it. Now that's a testimony.
text_fidelity_b: Bare Neckd Ice Cooling Towels for Athletes Sports Fitness Gym Yoga Hiking Travel Hot Flashes| Reusable Wrap Around Ice Pack

text_fidelity_a:
Trangia Fuel Bottle Headline pretty well sums it up. This bottle and pour spout is much easier to use than the soda bottle or HEET bottle I was using before. Pouring fuel into the Trangia burner is far easier, it won't come open when inside or strapped to the outside of my pack. This bottle is STURDY, I don't worry about puncturing it like I did with the soda bottles. The seals are meant for alcohol use, so no concerns about a seal on a soda bottle going wonky and spilling fuel(aka my coffee and non-crunchy pasta) when miles from civilization either.

Possible downside is weight. I'm not lugging the kitchen sink into the back country, but I also don't do long hikes and I'm not cutting the handle off my toothbrush to save 0.3 grams. If that's you, the soda bottle is probably a better bet.

These bottles will also work with gasoline and kerosene. US law changed and so this kind of bottle can't be advertised for gasoline use anymore, but it's exactly the same bottle from before the law change, and is still used with kero and gasoline in the rest of the world. YMMV, this is not medical or legal advice, insert standard disclaimer here, etc etc.

One last thought, the .3l bottle has been great for single day or overnight hikes and is of course the lightest. Longer than that and I'd want a bigger fuel bottle. We like our coffee and tea and boil a lot of water. If you're just heating up coffee water or something on a day hike, then as long as the O-ring seal in your burner cap is good you probably don't need to carry any extra fuel at all.

Five stars, wish I had bought it sooner.

Edit: Just bought the 1L version. Should have bought it when I bought the 0.3l version!
text_fidelity_b: Trangia Fuel Bottle
